thesis: This episode argues that Sherwin-Williams is a superior, durable business with exceptional growth characteristics that justify its premium valuation, effectively making it a bargain compared to peers. It highlights the company's unique distribution model, high market share, and resilience in downturns as key drivers of its outperformance over the S&P. The thesis suggests that while future returns may be more modest as the market appreciates such businesses, the company still has significant runway and a history of compounding earnings at 14% annually.

claims.claim: Sherwin-Williams is a great example of a company where everyday consumers might not appreciate just how great of a business and stock this has been.
claims.quote: This is Matt Russell, and today we are breaking down the paint giant Sherwin-Williams. Sherwin-Williams is a great example of a company where everyday consumers might not appreciate just how great of a business and stock this has been.

claims.claim: Over the last 20 years, the company has compounded earnings at 14% per year, and the stock has returned 26 times your investment compared to the S&P at five times.
claims.quote: Over the last 20 years, Sherman has compounded earnings at 14% per year. And over those 20 years, the stock has returned 26 times your investment. And that's compared to the S&P at five times your investment.

claims.claim: The company operates over 4,700 dedicated paint stores in North America, which is more than all the Home Depot's and Lowe's combined.
claims.quote: Sherwin operates over 4,700 dedicated paint stores in North America. That's more than all the Home Depot's and Lowe's combined. It's also more than half of all the dedicated paint stores in the country.

claims.claim: Paint sales are less influenced by change in interest rates, and they tend to hold up better in downturns than many other home improvement categories.
claims.quote: Therefore, paint sales are less influenced by change in interest rates, and they tend to hold up better in downturns than many other home improvement categories. Think about it as the affordable luxury of the home improvement category.

claims.claim: Sherwin-Williams controls roughly 65% of the architectural paint market, making it the dominant player.
claims.quote: Paints a highly consolidated industry, mostly by Sherwin-Williams, which controls roughly 65% of the market, followed by Masco's Bear, PPG, and Berkshire Hathaway is Benjamin Moore.

claims.claim: Sherwin-Williams dominates the professional paint market with a unique controlled distribution model and high customer loyalty.
claims.quote: Sherwin's entire business model is designed to make pro painters more productive and therefore more profitable. As a result, professional painter's are extremely loyal to Sherwin, prefering it over the number two brand Benjamin Moore by a margin of five to one.

claims.quote: Masco has high teens operating margins, which compares to Sherwin's paint stores group in the low 20s. And Masco has equally low cap-ex, of course, without even the need to open stores.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions Benjamin Moore's financials prior to Berkshire's acquisition showed high teens operating margins from selling paint through other stores.
claims.quote: And actually, the last time we got to look at Ben Morris financials financials, prior to Berkshire acquiring them, they also had high teens' operating margins by selling paint through other stores.

claims.claim: The speaker highlights that Sherwin purchased Valspar entirely with debt, avoiding equity issuance, which was a clear sign of long-term focus.
claims.quote: And rightfully so, Sherwin was able to purchase Valspar for over $11 billion entirely with debt. When you consider that Sherwin was a $30 billion market cap company at the time, this was a substantial deal to complete without having to issue stock.

claims.claim: The speaker views Sherwin-Williams as a bargain because its premium valuation relative to peers actually reflects a discount due to superior growth and durability.
claims.quote: Therefore, paying a modest premium to the market or peers for far superior growth in returns with less risk, it seemed like a bargain. And as such, Sherwin's stock has compounded well in excess of the market and those peers over time, suggesting that its, quote, unquote, premium valuation was actually a discount.

claims.claim: The speaker believes future stock returns may be more modest now because the market has developed greater appreciation for superior businesses like Sherwin.
claims.quote: Today, I do think the market has developed a greater appreciation for some truly superior businesses such as Sherwin, and as such, perhaps future stock returns may be more modest, given a higher starting point with regards to to valuation, which is now close to the 30 times earnings.
